source_note: All cases sourced from public OSHA.gov / DOL.gov press releases and eTools. Civilian shipyards only. No Navy mishap data included by design (see PASSDOWN.md, Section 7).

cases.shipyard: St. John's Ship Building, Palatka FL
cases.summary: Welder entered a 4x8 ft space in a ship's hull for fabrication work without the space being tested for oxygen content. Supervisor who went to assist was also overcome. Welder died of asphyxiation.
cases.root_cause: No pre-entry atmospheric testing for oxygen deficiency.
cases.osha_subpart: 1915 Subpart B - Confined and Enclosed Spaces

cases.shipyard: First Marine LLC, Calvert City KY
cases.summary: Explosion onboard a towboat during cutting/welding in an atmosphere containing flammable gases. 3 fatalities, 2 critical injuries. Five contractors cited (prime, insulation sub, two staffing agencies, one individual).
cases.root_cause: Hot work performed without testing for explosive atmosphere; confined space not tested before entry.
cases.osha_subpart: 1915 Subpart D - Welding, Cutting and Heating / Subpart B - Confined Spaces

cases.shipyard: Detyens Shipyards Inc., North Charleston SC
cases.summary: 41-year-old worker fell ~20 ft from an unguarded platform edge inside a gas tank aboard a Naval Ship undergoing fuel piping work. Co-workers were waiting for him to descend a ladder.
cases.root_cause: No guardrails on platform edge; inadequate lighting; no hard hats required for workers below overhead activity.
cases.osha_subpart: 1915 Subpart E - Guarding of Deck Openings and Edges

cases.shipyard: Detyens Shipyards Inc., North Charleston SC
cases.summary: Employee fatally struck by a shackle during a lifting operation while positioned between a guardrail and a rudder shaft being lifted.
cases.root_cause: No fall protection system in use; employee allowed in a caught-between hazard zone during a lift.

cases.shipyard: Detyens Shipyards Inc., North Charleston SC
cases.summary: Comprehensive OSHA inspection (Regional Emphasis Program on Maritime Industries) resulted in 1 repeated, 13 serious, 1 other-than-serious citation for fall, electrical, and amputation hazards.
cases.root_cause: Systemic/repeat noncompliance pattern at the same facility -- valuable as a longitudinal case rather than a single incident.

cases.shipyard: South Marine Systems LLC, Port of Ashtabula OH
cases.summary: Fire erupted while workers welded to remove paint from a cargo hold aboard the commercial vessel Cuyahoga. Crewmembers who had been working below the cargo hold were on lunch break at the time and avoided being trapped below decks by the fire.
cases.root_cause: No designated competent person to identify hot work hazards, no marine chemist certificate to test for hazardous atmospheres, and no procedure to assess conditions once small fires began.
cases.osha_subpart: 1915 Subpart D - Welding, Cutting and Heating / Subpart B - Confined and Enclosed Spaces

cases.shipyard: Guam Industrial Services Inc. (Guam Shipyard), Santa Rita, Guam
cases.summary: A rigger was fatally struck when a barge-mounted crane's cable snapped while lowering a 100-foot gantry crane leg that exceeded the crane's rated capacity. The load swung after the boom bent and the cable snapped, striking the rigger.
cases.root_cause: Management proceeded with a lift exceeding the crane's rated capacity over workers' objections (workers had proposed cutting the load into pieces first), and failed to ensure the crane operator was trained, certified, and evaluated.
cases.osha_subpart: 1915 Subpart G - Gear and Equipment for Rigging and Materials Handling

over_the_side DROPPED as a standalone case-citation target (architecture review + SME call, 2026-07-24, see MIGRATION.md Phase 4 amendment): under 29 CFR 1915, over-water fall hazards are legally captured under Fall Protection (Subpart I / 1915.73), not a separate civilian OSHA case classification -- standalone over-the-side tracking is a Naval/NSTM underway operational convention, out of scope for this project. The SSA Pacific longshoreman case that was previously considered and excluded (marine cargo handling under 1917/1918, not 1915) stays excluded for the same original reason. Future over-water staging cases should be sourced and tagged fall_protection instead.

confined_space needs more cases beyond St. John's Ship Building -- the HW-ASHTABULA-2024 fire also involved a confined/enclosed space but is filed under hot_work since that was the proximate hazard; a search focused specifically on confined-space entry/atmosphere-testing citations at named shipyards (not generic OSHA training videos, which don't name a real incident) is still needed.
fall_protection is comparatively well covered (3 cases, all Detyens) but all three are the same shipyard -- a case from a different facility would strengthen this category.
